subject.title: Install ClawHub packages for new Claw agents

question: Should the experimental Claw lifecycle be permitted to install or reuse process-wide plugins from a consented Claw package, rather than limiting this slice to workspace-scoped skills until a separate host-grant model exists?
rationale: The code deliberately makes plugin installation shared-host rather than agent-isolated; deciding whether exact-plan consent is sufficient for that authority is product and security-boundary policy, not a mechanical repair.

options.title: Approve the explicit shared-host model
options.body: Accept exact-plan consent for shared plugin mutation after the contributor supplies current-head live proof for install, reuse, conflict, and compensation.

options.title: Ship skills only
options.body: Retain workspace-scoped skill installation and defer all plugin mutation until maintainers define a separate host-level grant.

options.title: Pause the package-owner slice
options.body: Defer the entire package lifecycle until the broader Claw RFC and ownership model are settled.

recommendation.title: Approve the explicit shared-host model
recommendation.body: Accept exact-plan consent for shared plugin mutation after the contributor supplies current-head live proof for install, reuse, conflict, and compensation.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review directly frames the user-facing shared-host versus workspace-scoped capability boundary that requires an explicit policy choice.
